items.informal_name: Lower Bound for Polynomial Evaluation at Rational Points
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] {f : Polynomial ℤ} {a b : ℤ},
  0 < b →
    Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f) ≠ 0 →
      1 ≤ ↑b ^ f.natDegree * |Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f)|
items.informal_description: For any linearly ordered field $ K $ with strict ordered ring structure, given a non-zero polynomial $ f \in \mathbb{Z}[X] $, integers $ a, b $ with $ b > 0 $, and assuming $ f\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) \neq 0 $, it holds that $ 1 \leq b^{\deg(f)} \cdot \left| f\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) \right| $, where $ \deg(f) $ denotes the natural degree of $ f $.

items.informal_name: Denominator Divides Leading Coefficient for Roots in Fraction Ring
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A]
  [inst_3 : Field K] [inst_4 : Algebra A K] [inst_5 : IsFractionRing A K] {p : Polynomial A} {r : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval r) p = 0 → ↑(IsFractionRing.den A r) ∣ p.leadingCoeff
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ A $ and an element $ r $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of $ A $, if $ r $ is a root of $ p $ (i.e., $ \text{aeval}(r, p) = 0 $), then the denominator $ \text{den}(r) $ of $ r $ (as defined in the fraction ring) divides the leading coefficient of $ p $. This generalizes the classical Rational Root Theorem to fraction rings of commutative semirings.

items.informal_name: Denominators Clearable Given Bounded Polynomial Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring K] {i : R →+* K} {b : R} {bi : K} (N : ℕ)
  (a : R), bi * i b = 1 → ∀ (f : Polynomial R), f.natDegree ≤ N → DenomsClearable a b N f i
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ f $ with natural degree $ \leq N $, there exist elements $ D \in R $ and $ \beta \in K $ such that $ \beta \cdot i(b) = 1 $ and $ i(D) = i(b)^N \cdot \text{eval}_{i(a)\beta}(f^i) $, where $ f^i $ denotes the polynomial obtained by applying the ring homomorphism $ i $ to each coefficient of $ f $.

items.type: {R : Type u} → [inst : Ring R] → R → Polynomial R → ℕ
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ with decidable equality, the function $\operatorname{rootMultiplicity}(a, p) $ returns the largest natural number $ n $ such that the linear factor $ X - a $ divides the polynomial $ p $ exactly $ n $ times. If $ p $ is the zero polynomial, it returns $ 0 $. This is computed by finding the minimal $ n $ where $ (X - a)^{n+1} $ does not divide $ p $, leveraging the finite multiplicity property of linear factors in polynomial rings.
